requirements.requirement: Join node2 and node3's separate segments into a single L2 domain sharing one subnet
requirements.summary: Baseline isolation was proven (matching-subnet IPs assigned on both nodes, ping failed with Destination Host Unreachable before bridging). After creating br0 on node1 spanning eth1/eth2 and configuring persistent static IPs 192.168.50.11/.12 via nmcli, node2 and node3 successfully pinged each other on the shared 192.168.50.0/24 subnet.

requirements.requirement: node1 forwards frames transparently at layer 2 rather than acting as a routed hop
requirements.summary: Ping between node2/node3 showed TTL=64 (unmodified, i.e. no hop decrement expected from routing), arping/ip-neigh on node2 resolved node3's actual interface MAC (not node1's), and node1's bridge fdb table showed each peer's real MAC learned on its correct bridge port — direct evidence of L2 bridging, not IP routing.

requirements.requirement: Bridge configuration and connectivity persist across node1 reboot (survivability)
requirements.summary: Healthy baseline (boot_id, forwarding state) was captured before node1's reboot; a persisted /etc/network/interfaces.d/br0 config was written beforehand; after the reboot the boot_id changed, bridge link show confirmed eth1/eth2 auto-rejoined br0 in forwarding state, and node2<->node3 connectivity was re-verified — a complete before/disruption/after transition was directly observed.

requirements.requirement: Mandatory provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all three managed nodes
requirements.summary: Each of node1, node2, node3 has a captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy state, a restart acknowledgement, connection disruption during the restart window, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and recovered service state (bridge forwarding on node1; persisted static IP and connectivity on node2/node3). These boot_id transitions match exactly the fixed after-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots for all three nodes, providing an independent cross-check.

overall_summary: The executor joined node2 and node3's isolated segments into a single L2 domain via a Linux bridge (br0) on node1, with strong direct evidence that node1 forwards frames at L2 (unmodified TTL, real peer MACs resolved, correct fdb port learning) rather than routing. Bridge configuration was persisted to survive reboot and this was directly verified through an actual node1 reboot showing automatic bridge recreation. The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was completed on all three nodes with pre/post boot-identity, disruption, and recovery evidence that is consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found.
limitations: The `ip -br link show eth1 eth2 br0` command in the post-node1-reboot check (cmd-668658b6b9b641e6) errored with a syntax issue, though the accompanying `bridge link show` in the same command succeeded and provided the needed confirmation, so this does not materially weaken the evidence.
Bridge persistence file was written but a full node1 cold reboot was the only direct proof of survivability observed; no second independent reboot cycle was performed to rule out one-off recovery.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands trace to task requirements: bridge creation/deletion-recreation on node1 (cmd-8051416569934907), transient `ip addr add` on node2/node3 used to establish and later confirm the pre-bridge baseline (cmd-ff4b3329d29c436e, cmd-01754e17039f4f2d) were superseded by the persistent nmcli static-IP configuration (cmd-cf5fd8bc56134e5d, cmd-90fa38f7fa6f4a9f), which was itself necessary because NetworkManager was reconciling away the manual IPs. The bridge persistence file (cmd-8e08942439304cac) and all three reboots are directly tied to the task and the mandatory restart protocol. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary mutations were introduced; the pre-existing SONiC failed services (system-health.service, watchdog-control.service) and dummy-bridge master were present before the executor acted and are unchanged after.
